target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures define Loans Held-for-Sale (LHFS) as loans intended for sale in the foreseeable future, carried at the lower of aggregate cost or fair value.

Both disclosures address the election of the fair value option for specific Loans Held-for-Sale, explicitly mentioning residential mortgage LHFS.

Both disclosures explain the accounting treatment for loan origination costs for LHFS carried at the lower of cost or fair value, stating they are capitalized and recognized upon sale.

comparisons.peer_topic: Classification and reporting of held-for-investment loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans held-for-investment are reported at outstanding principal balances net of unearned income and unamortized deferred fees, with specific treatments for credit card receivables and loans under the fair value option. Loan origination fees and direct origination costs are deferred and recognized over the life of the related loans.
comparisons.comparison: While Citi's disclosure (c_2024_8_D067) primarily addresses Loans Held-for-Investment (HFI) rather than Held-for-Sale (LHFS), it provides context on the general treatment of loan origination costs. Citi states that loan origination fees and certain direct origination costs are generally deferred and recognized as adjustments to income over the lives of the related loans. This contrasts with BAC's LHFS treatment, where costs are capitalized and recognized upon sale, but establishes the baseline policy for other loan categories that differs based on the holding intent (HFI vs LHFS).

sentences.text: Loan origination costs for LHFS carried at the lower of cost or fair value are capitalized as part of the carrying value of the loans and, upon the sale of a loan, are recognized as part of the gain or loss in noninterest income.
Loan origination fees and certain direct origination costs are generally deferred and recognized as adjustments to income over the lives of the related loans.

peer_results.rationale: Goldman Sachs' provided disclosures focus on the general classification of loans (held for investment vs. sale) and lending commitments, but do not contain specific sentences detailing the capitalization or deferral mechanics of loan origination costs for LHFS comparable to BAC's detailed policy. gs_2024_8_D215 states LHFS are accounted for at the lower of cost or fair value but lacks the specific origination cost treatment detail. gs_2024_8_D381 discusses lending commitments, which are derivative-like or off-balance sheet commitments, not the LHFS asset class itself.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting for deferred fees and purchase price adjustments for loans held-for-sale
comparisons.peer_summary: Loan origination fees, costs, discounts, and premiums are deferred in a contra loan account until the loan is sold, where they serve as adjustments to the loan basis for determining fair value adjustments or gains/losses at sale.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose the accounting for loan origination costs specifically for LHFS. BAC capitalizes these costs into the carrying value, recognizing them as part of the gain or loss in noninterest income upon sale. JPM similarly defers loan origination fees or costs in a contra loan account until sale, noting that these deferrals are included in the periodic determination of lower of cost or fair value adjustments and/or the gain or loss recognized at the time of sale. The core treatment of capitalizing/deferring costs to adjust the gain/loss upon sale is consistent between the two.

sentences.text: Loan origination costs for LHFS carried at the lower of cost or fair value are capitalized as part of the carrying value of the loans and, upon the sale of a loan, are recognized as part of the gain or loss in noninterest income.
Loan origination fees or costs and purchase price discounts or premiums are deferred in a contra loan account until the related loan is sold.

The deferred fees or costs and discounts or premiums are an adjustment to the basis of the loan and therefore are included in the periodic determination of the lower of cost or fair value adjustments and/or the gain or loss recognized at the time of sale.

comparisons.peer_topic: Interest income and fee recognition for loans held for sale
comparisons.peer_summary: Interest income is accrued based on contractual rates. Loan origination fees, costs, and purchase price discounts or premiums are deferred as adjustments to the loan's cost basis until sale, affecting the determination of lower of cost or fair value adjustments and gains or losses at the time of sale.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS describe the treatment of loan origination costs for Loans Held-for-Sale (LHFS) carried at the lower of cost or fair value. BAC states that origination costs are capitalized into the loan's carrying value and recognized as part of gain or loss upon sale. Similarly, MS states that origination fees or costs are deferred as an adjustment to the loan's cost basis until sale, where they are included in the determination of lower of cost or fair value adjustments and the gain or loss recognized at the time of sale. Both disclosures reflect the same accounting mechanic of deferring costs to adjust the basis/gain/loss upon disposal.

sentences.text: Loan origination costs for LHFS carried at the lower of cost or fair value are capitalized as part of the carrying value of the loans and, upon the sale of a loan, are recognized as part of the gain or loss in noninterest income.

Loan origination fees or costs and purchase price discounts or premiums are deferred as an adjustment to the loan's cost basis until the related loan is sold and, as such, are included in the periodic determination of the lower of cost or fair value adjustments and the gain or loss recognized at the time of sale.
